source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Activity entry point / LAUNCH_ACTIVITY and ready then authorize lifecycle
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: With Activities enabled, the user invokes the App Launcher entry point or an interaction responds with callback type 12. SDK construction starts a handshake; READY resolves ready(), then authorization and authentication follow. READY is connection state, not membership proof.
source_context_rows.heading: Launching Activities; Entry Point Command; Interaction Response; Activity Lifecycle
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Which authoritative server evidence proves exact launch or current presence?

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Proxy/WebSocket, unsupported WebRTC, patchUrlMappings, client trust, and iframe SameSite/Partitioned cookies
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Proxy supports WebSockets while WebRTC is unsupported. Mapping helper changes fetch, WebSocket and XHR globals and may have side effects. Client identity/channel data can be falsified and trusted facts require server API checks. Cookie guidance specifies full app domain and SameSite=None Partitioned for iframe requests.
source_context_rows.heading: Activity Proxy Considerations; Using External Resources; Trusting Client Data; Using Cookies
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Actual CSP, mappings, WSS and cookie behavior per client remain untested.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Mapping prefix/target format and order, CSP API exceptions, platform toggles
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Portal maps prefixes to targets without protocol, targets directories, and orders longer overlapping paths before shorter. CSP permits listed Discord API and CDN paths without proxy mappings. Shelf display depends on platform checkboxes.
source_context_rows.heading: Launch your application from the Discord Client; URL Mapping; Prefix/Target formatting rules; Exceptions
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Actual portal configuration and deployed routing require tests.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Web/desktop default, iOS/Android toggles, safe areas, thermal availability versus supported versions
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Web/desktop launch is default; platform checkboxes enable or disable Web/iOS/Android. Safe-area inset example and thermal-state subscriptions are documented; Android thermal updates require Android 10 or higher. This is not a tested Guildboard client-version matrix.
source_context_rows.heading: Supported Platforms: Web, iOS, Android; Mobile Safe Areas; Mobile Thermal States
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Exact supported Discord, OS, browser and device versions remain unknown.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Cache busting, rate limits, and INVALID_COMMAND on older clients
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Non-HTML assets need cache-busting; proxy strips cache headers from HTML. Both client and server should respect API limits. New commands typically require newer clients; unsupported older clients return INVALID_COMMAND.
source_context_rows.heading: Cache Busting; Handling Rate Limits; Backward Compatibility / New Commands
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Actual compatibility and recovery require versioned client tests.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: AuthorizeRequest optional state/S256 challenge and documented code-only AuthorizeResponse
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: The request table marks state and code_challenge optional and code_challenge_method optional S256; the response table lists code. These declarations establish neither runtime PKCE enforcement nor an echoed state.
source_context_rows.heading: AuthorizeRequest; AuthorizeResponse
source_context_rows.residual_questions: SDK/provider transaction and response binding, state propagation and verifier enforcement remain unknown.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Token form encoding, redirect state, PKCE code flow and scopes versus unknown SDK postMessage binding
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Token and revocation endpoints require form encoding; redirect flow returns previously sent state for validation and code for exchange, while some scopes need approval. Production guidance recommends code grant with PKCE. This redirect description does not establish SDK postMessage response binding.
source_context_rows.heading: OAuth2 URLs; OAuth2 Scopes; State and Security; Authorization Code Grant; Implicit Grant
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Approved scopes and actual SDK/provider binding and exchange behavior remain open.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: identify current user and guilds.members.read selected-guild membership versus guild listing
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: User fields list identify; the selected-guild current-user member endpoint requires guilds.members.read, whereas current-user guild listing returns partial guilds and requires guilds. The endpoints have distinct purposes.
source_context_rows.heading: User Object; Get Current User Guilds; Get Current User Guild Member
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Actual granted scopes and selected-guild access require controlled tests.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Guild member roles, role definitions and privileged list intent; one member need not be listed
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Member roles are role IDs; guild role endpoint returns role objects. Get Guild Member returns one specified member; List Guild Members explicitly requires GUILD_MEMBERS privileged intent. This does not establish every authorization prerequisite for the single-member route.
source_context_rows.heading: Guild Member Object; Get Guild Member; List Guild Members; Get Guild Roles
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Validate actual endpoint permissions and role freshness in controlled guilds.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Channel guild association and permission overwrites, not bot visibility as user presence
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Channel object fields include optional guild_id and member/role permission_overwrites; guild_id may be absent in some gateway dispatches. These fields are policy inputs, not proof of user access, launch, or current presence.
source_context_rows.heading: Channel Object
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Determine a trusted source and actual user access and presence separately.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Role/overwrite permissions, string BigInteger representation, ADMINISTRATOR and tenant boundary
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Discord combines guild roles with channel/member overwrites; permissions are serialized as strings and Big Integer handling is recommended. ADMINISTRATOR bypasses Discord channel overwrites; Guildboard tenant isolation is an application contract and cannot be inferred away from that Discord permission.
source_context_rows.heading: Permissions introduction; Bitwise Permission Flags; Permission Overwrites
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Implement and verify Guildboard policy and tenant fences independently.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Member/role events and privileged intent approval; bot token is not intent approval
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: GUILDS intent includes role events; GUILD_MEMBERS includes member add/update/remove. Privileged intents require portal enablement; verified apps and other specified thresholds require approval/review. An unconfigured or unapproved privileged intent can close the connection.
source_context_rows.heading: Gateway Intents; List of Intents; Privileged Intents; Privileged Intent Access Review
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Actual app intent approval, applicable threshold and event delivery remain unknown.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: Actual Retry-After, route and global rate-limit guidance
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Limits are variable; parse response headers instead of hardcoding. Routes can share buckets and depend on top-level resources; global limits are independent. On 429 use Retry-After or retry_after to decide delay.
source_context_rows.heading: Rate limits introduction; Header Format; Exceeding A Rate Limit; Global Rate Limit
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Implement bounded retry and validate behavior against real traffic.

source_context_rows.exact_scoped_claim: RFC 9700 CSRF, code injection, PKCE and redirect binding; not Discord SDK proof
source_context_rows.context_paraphrase: Authorization servers MUST use exact string matching for pre-registered redirect URIs, except for localhost port numbers in native apps. Clients MUST prevent CSRF; they MAY rely on PKCE for CSRF protection when authorization server support is established, and in OpenID Connect flows nonce provides CSRF protection. Otherwise, one-time state CSRF tokens securely bound to the user agent MUST be used. To prevent authorization code injection and misuse, public clients MUST use PKCE and confidential clients are RECOMMENDED to use it; confidential OpenID Connect clients MAY instead use nonce and the respective ID Token claim with additional precautions. The PKCE challenge or OpenID Connect nonce MUST be transaction-specific and securely bound to the client and initiating user agent. Authorization servers MUST support PKCE, enforce correct verifier use at the token endpoint when a valid challenge was sent, and mitigate downgrade by accepting a token request containing a verifier only if a challenge was present in the authorization request. These RFC requirements do not establish Discord implementation or provider enforcement.
source_context_rows.heading: 2.1 Protecting Redirect-Based Flows; 2.1.1 Authorization Code Grant; 4.1 Insufficient Redirection URI Validation
source_context_rows.residual_questions: Verify provider enforcement and SDK response binding in the actual flow.
